AquaPure Beverages - Q3 2024 Earnings Call Transcript

Operator:
Good morning, and welcome to the AquaPure Beverages Q3 2024 Earnings Conference Call. All participants are in a listen-only mode. After the speakers' presentation, there will be a question-and-answer session. During the Q&A, please press star then one on your telephone keypad if you would like to ask a question. As a reminder, this conference is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the call over to Sarah Johnson, Head of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Sarah Johnson (Head of Investor Relations):
Thank you, operator. Good morning, everyone, and thank you for joining us today to discuss AquaPure Beverages' Q3 2024 results. Joining me on the call are Mike Thompson, Chief Executive Officer; Lisa Chen, Chief Financial Officer; Raj Patel, Chief Growth Officer; and Elena Rodriguez, Chief Supply Chain Officer.

Before we begin, I would like to remind you that this call may contain forward-looking statements. Please refer to our SEC filings for a discussion of the factors that could cause actual results to differ materially from these statements.

With that, I'll turn the call over to Mike Thompson.

Mike Thompson (CEO):
Thank you, Sarah, and good morning, everyone. We are pleased to report our results for Q3 2024. We delivered strong performance despite ongoing macroeconomic headwinds and inflationary pressures.

Today, I'll be focusing on six key areas: progress on sustainability initiatives and goals, updates on M&A activity and portfolio management, EPS guidance and key assumptions, EBITDA margin performance and key factors, e-commerce sales growth and contribution to total revenue, and organic revenue growth overall and by region.

First, regarding progress on sustainability initiatives and goals: We've advanced significantly across our four pillars—planet positive operations, sustainable sourcing, circular packaging, and regenerative communities—reducing water use, boosting renewables, and hitting responsible sourcing targets ahead of schedule.

Second, concerning updates on M&A activity and portfolio management: We've completed strategic acquisitions like our plant-based dairy bolt-on and divested non-core assets, reshaping our portfolio toward high-ROIC health and wellness segments while advancing a robust pipeline.

Third, in terms of EPS guidance and key assumptions: We're raising our full-year outlook, supported by pricing discipline, productivity savings, and regional momentum in premium categories.

Fourth, looking at EBITDA margin performance and key factors: Margins expanded meaningfully through pricing, mix shifts, and supply chain efficiencies, outpacing input inflation.

Fifth, reviewing e-commerce sales growth and contribution to total revenue: This channel surged, now a core revenue driver at over 20% of sales, with strong growth in DTC and marketplaces.

Sixth, analyzing organic revenue growth overall and by region: We achieved solid acceleration globally, led by North America and APAC, through pricing, mix, and volume gains in functional beverages and snacks.

Overall, we are confident in our ability to navigate the current environment and deliver long-term value for our shareholders.

Now, I'll turn the call over to Lisa Chen to provide more detail on our financial results.

Lisa Chen (CFO):
Thank you, Mike. As Mike mentioned, we achieved solid results in Q3 2024. Net sales were $1.45 billion, representing an 8% increase year-over-year. Gross margin was 38.8%, impacted by elevated input costs like cocoa and dairy but offset by productivity gains and pricing actions. Operating income was $278 million, and earnings per share were $1.52. We are managing our costs effectively and continue to invest in key growth initiatives.

Our balance sheet remains strong with $1.1 billion in cash and marketable securities. We are committed to returning value to shareholders through dividends and share repurchases.

Thank you, Mike, and good morning, everyone. As we continue to deliver strong financial results—with adjusted EPS up 12% year-over-year and organic revenue growth of 8%—I want to spend some time updating you on our progress against our sustainability roadmap. At AquaPure Beverages, sustainability isn't just a checkbox; it's a core driver of long-term value creation in the Food & Beverage sector. With escalating climate risks, tightening regulations like the EU's Corporate Sustainability Reporting Directive and California's SB 253, and consumer preferences shifting—Nielsen data shows 78% of global consumers now prioritize sustainable brands—we're embedding ESG principles across our operations to fuel margin expansion, de-risk our $4.2 billion supply chain, and capture premium pricing in high-growth categories like plant-based juices and low-sugar functional beverages.

Let me break this down by our four key pillars: Planet Positive Operations, Sustainable Sourcing, Circular Packaging, and Regenerative Communities. We've made measurable strides since our 2023 baseline, validated by third-party audits from SGS and the Science Based Targets initiative, and we're on track to hit our 2030 Science-Based Targets, including a 50% absolute reduction in Scope 1 and 2 GHG emissions and 25% for Scope 3.

First, Planet Positive Operations. Water stewardship remains our top priority in an industry where beverages account for 70% of global packaged water use. We've reduced our absolute water withdrawal by 18% year-over-year to 1.2 billion cubic meters, surpassing our 15% target, thanks to advanced membrane bioreactor tech at our flagship plant in Monterrey, Mexico, which now recycles 85% of process water—mirroring efficiencies seen at PepsiCo's Guadalajara facility. In energy, our pivot to renewables hit 42% of our global portfolio, up from 28% last year, with 250 MW of solar PPAs secured in India and the U.S. Southwest. This drove a 22% drop in Scope 1 and 2 emissions to 450,000 metric tons CO2e, while slashing energy costs by $15 million annually. Regionally, Europe leads at 65% renewable energy coverage, compliant with the REPowerEU plan, while APAC—our fastest-growing market at 15% revenue CAGR—saw a 30% emissions cut via grid-tied solar at our Vietnam PET bottling lines.

On Sustainable Sourcing, we're at 72% responsibly sourced key ingredients, up from 55% in 2023, targeting 90% by 2030. For sugarcane, 95% of our 450,000 metric tons now comes from Bonsucro-certified farms in Brazil's Center-West region, reducing deforestation risk amid the Amazon Soy Moratorium's ripple effects. Fruit sourcing for our AquaPure Organic line—think Valencia oranges and Peruvian mangoes—reached 88% sustainable via Rainforest Alliance partnerships, yielding a 12% cost hedge against volatile commodity prices, up 25% YTD per Bloomberg. In cocoa for our emerging plant-based chocolate milks, we've enrolled 15,000 smallholder farmers in Côte d'Ivoire under a Cocoa Life-inspired program, boosting yields 20% through agroforestry and cutting child labor incidents to zero per audits. This not only mitigates Scope 3 hotspots, which comprise 92% of our footprint, but supports premium SKU growth—our sustainable portfolio now drives 35% of North American revenues, with 15% price premiums akin to Coca-Cola's Sprite Zero Sugar success.

Circular Packaging is accelerating, with 68% of our 2.8 billion units sold now recyclable, reusable, or compostable—exceeding our 60% 2025 goal. We've fully transitioned to 100% rPET for our 500ml AquaPure Spring bottles in the U.S. and EU, partnering with Loop Industries for chemical recycling at scale. Aluminum cans, now 45% of volume, feature infinitely recyclable designs with 50% PCR content, reducing virgin material use by 28% and aligning with the global aluminum beverage can recycling rate push toward 80% by 2030 per CANPACK benchmarks. In APAC, where plastic waste regulations like India's single-use ban bite hardest, we've rolled out 200 million paper-based multipack carriers, diverting 5,000 tons from landfills. This initiative saved $22 million in resin costs amid PET price spikes and boosted brand loyalty—our Net Promoter Score for eco-packaging jumped 14 points to 72.

Finally, Regenerative Communities. Beyond compliance, we're investing $50 million over five years in biodiversity projects, including 10,000 hectares of regenerative agriculture pilots in California's Central Valley for almond milk alternatives—partnering with General Mills on cover cropping to sequester 15,000 tons of CO2 annually. In LATAM, our $10 million water recharge program in São Paulo replenished 200 million cubic meters, supporting local aquifers strained by El Niño droughts. Socially, diverse supplier spend hit 25% of procurement, $450 million, with a focus on women-led farms in Kenya for our herbal tea infusions.

Strategically, these efforts are yielding tangible ROI: sustainability-linked financing at 75 bps below our benchmark curve via our $500 million green bond, and a 20% reduction in insurance premiums from enhanced climate resilience modeling. Looking ahead, with ESG funds pouring $1.7 trillion into F&B per Morningstar, we're positioning AquaPure as the sector leader—much like Unilever's 15% sustainable growth premium. Risks remain, like Scope 3 supplier traceability under upcoming ISSB standards, but our blockchain pilot with IBM Food Trust covers 40% of Tier 1 suppliers already.

Next, on updates to our M&A activity and portfolio management. Good afternoon, everyone. As we continue to execute on our 'Power Brands, Precision Portfolio' strategy, I'd like to provide a detailed update. In an industry facing persistent commodity inflation—up 12% year-over-year on key inputs like cocoa, dairy, and edible oils per the latest Rabobank Food & Agribusiness report—along with shifting consumer preferences toward health-focused, sustainable, and premium products, our disciplined approach to capital allocation has delivered strong results. We've realized $450 million in total enterprise value from transactions year-to-date, while optimizing our portfolio for higher ROIC segments.

Let me start with recent M&A completions. In August, we closed our $620 million acquisition of PureHarvest Organics, a leading U.S.-based producer of plant-based dairy alternatives with brands like GreenMoo almond and oat milks. This bolt-on deal enhances our presence in the $25 billion global plant-based dairy category, which is growing at 15% CAGR according to NielsenIQ data. PureHarvest brings immediate scale: $180 million in trailing twelve-month revenue, 22% adjusted EBITDA margins, and a robust distribution network covering 45% of U.S. grocery chains, including key accounts at Kroger and Whole Foods. Synergies are tracking ahead of our $75 million three-year target, driven by $30 million in procurement savings from integrating their vertically integrated almond orchards with our existing nut supply chain in California. We've already realized 40% of those savings in Q3 through optimized hedging against almond price volatility, which spiked 18% this quarter.

Complementing this, in July we divested our legacy canned soup business—Heritage Hearty—to Campbell Soup Company for $285 million in cash. This non-core asset generated just $95 million in revenue with single-digit margins, weighed down by declining volumes in a commoditized category shrinking 3% annually per IRI data. The sale achieved a 1.8x EBITDA multiple, unlocking $220 million in net proceeds after taxes, which we've redeployed into high-growth areas. Post-divestiture, our exposure to low-growth packaged soups drops to under 2% of total portfolio revenue, improving our overall organic growth profile by 150 basis points.

On the pipeline front, we're advancing several opportunities aligned with our three strategic pillars: health & wellness, premium snacking, and emerging markets expansion. We remain active with $1.2 billion in dry powder from our recent $800 million bond issuance at 4.25%—a testament to our investment-grade balance sheet with net debt to EBITDA at 2.1x. Key targets include a tuck-in acquisition in Asia-Pacific for functional beverages, where we're eyeing a bolt-on in Thailand's kombucha and adaptogen space to bolster our VitaGlow line amid 20% category growth driven by Gen Z demand. We've also signed LOIs for two smaller deals totaling $150 million: a Brazilian superfruit puree supplier to fuel our smoothie platform and a European clean-label snack bar maker, capitalizing on the 28% CAGR in protein-fortified snacks per Euromonitor.

Regionally, North America remains our M&A epicenter, accounting for 65% of deal flow, fueled by premiumization trends—our acquired assets here are projected to add 400 basis points to U.S. segment margins through cross-selling into our 15,000-store footprint. In EMEA, regulatory headwinds like the EU's Green Deal packaging mandates have tempered activity, but we're progressing a €120 million divestiture of a low-margin private-label yogurt packager in Germany, targeting closure by year-end to fund sustainability tech upgrades. APAC is a bright spot: post our 2023 acquisition of SingaBev's ready-to-drink teas, we're seeing 18% revenue uplift from e-commerce channels like Tmall and Shopee, and our pipeline here emphasizes halal-certified products to tap Indonesia's $15 billion Muslim consumer market growing at 10% annually.

Turning to portfolio management, we've made significant progress reshaping our 45-brand portfolio toward high-conviction categories. Health & wellness now represents 38% of revenue—up from 25% two years ago—delivering 12% organic growth versus the company average of 7%. We've divested or wound down $400 million in underperforming assets YTD, including marginal bakery mixes and sugary cereals, achieving a portfolio ROIC uplift from 11% to 14.2%. Key technical initiatives underpinning this include our AI-driven Portfolio Optimizer platform, powered by Palantir Foundry, which models 5,000 SKUs across 20 demand scenarios. This has identified $120 million in annual cost opportunities, such as rationalizing 15% of our legacy CPG SKUs with duplicative formulations.

Sustainability is woven into our core: all M&A targets must score 80+ on our ESG scorecard, emphasizing Scope 3 emissions tracking via blockchain provenance for cocoa and palm oil—critical amid 25% tariff risks on imports per USDA forecasts. We've also launched a $50 million venture arm, AquaVentures, investing in agritech like precision fermentation for dairy proteins, mirroring partnerships seen with Nestlé and Perfect Day.

Looking forward, we expect M&A to contribute 2-3 points to FY24 EPS growth, with full-year synergies exceeding $120 million. Our leverage target remains 2.0-2.5x, supporting 10-12% CAGR in adjusted EPS through the cycle. This positions AquaPure to outperform in a consolidating industry where majors like PepsiCo and Mondelez are paying 12-15x EBITDA for premium assets.

Now, I'll turn to our full-year 2024 outlook, where we're raising our adjusted EPS guidance to a range of $5.85 to $6.05, up from our prior range of $5.65 to $5.85. This represents approximately 12% growth at the midpoint versus 2023's adjusted EPS of $5.22, reflecting the strength of our core brands, disciplined pricing actions, and productivity gains outpacing input cost inflation. For context, this guidance excludes approximately $0.15 of dilution from our recent acquisition of HealthySip Brands, which bolsters our better-for-you beverage portfolio amid rising consumer demand for low-sugar, functional drinks.

Let me walk you through the key assumptions underpinning this updated guidance, which are grounded in our rolling 12-month forecast model, incorporating the latest commodity curves, FX rates, and consumer tracking data from Nielsen and IRI.

Revenue Outlook: We're now guiding to full-year net revenue growth of 5% to 7%, with organic net revenue growth—our preferred metric excluding FX, M&A, and divestitures—at the top end of 4% to 6%. This breaks down to pricing of 2.5% to 3.5%, volume/mix of 1% to 2.5%, and constant-currency tailwinds of about 50 basis points.

Pricing Discipline: We've embedded mid-single-digit pricing across our portfolio, similar to what we've seen from peers like PepsiCo in their North American convenient foods segment. This is sustainable given sticky inflation in key inputs—wheat up 8% YoY, cocoa futures still 40% elevated versus pre-2023 levels due to West African supply disruptions, and dairy costs +5% on stronger global demand. However, our forward contracts cover 85% of 2024 needs, mitigating volatility.

Volume/Mix Tailwinds: Early momentum in health-focused SKUs is driving mix, with plant-based snacks (e.g., our NutriBar line, up 15% in Q2) and zero-sugar beverages (like FreshQuench Zero) offsetting soft volumes in legacy carbonated soft drinks, down mid-single digits as consumers shift to premium hydration options. Our innovation pipeline—10 new launches planned for H2, including collagen-infused ready-to-drink coffees—targets the $25B global functional beverage market, growing at 8% CAGR per Euromonitor.

Gross Margin Expansion: We expect full-year adjusted gross margins of 38.5% to 39.5%, a 150 bps improvement versus 2023, driven by $450 million in supply chain productivity savings. Key initiatives include our "Zero Waste 2025" program, leveraging AI-optimized yield management in aseptic packaging lines, which delivered 2% yield gains in Q2 across dairy and plant-based plants. Transition to regional sourcing hubs in Southeast Asia for spices and tropical fruits, reducing ocean freight costs by 12% amid Red Sea disruptions. This more than offsets 3% to 4% input cost inflation, with cocoa hedges expiring favorably in Q4.

Operating Expenses and Profitability: SG&A as a percentage of revenue is guided at 24% to 25%, flat YoY as a percent, with absolute growth of 6% tied to marketing reinvestment behind core brands like CrispWave chips and PureHarvest juices. We're targeting adjusted operating income growth of 9% to 11%, flowing through to an EBITDA margin of 19.5% to 20.5%. Interest expense is assumed at $220 million, incorporating our recent $500 million bond issuance at 4.75% to refinance maturing debt, and an effective tax rate of 23.5%, stable despite R&D tax credits from our precision fermentation pilots for alt-proteins.

Regional Commentary:
- North America (65% of sales): Low-double-digit organic growth, fueled by snacking strength—our savory portfolio gained 2.3 share points in IRI tracked channels versus Mondelez and Kellogg. Health halo from reduced-sodium reformulations is resonating, though we're monitoring private label pressure in value channels.
- Europe/MEA (20%): Mid-single-digit growth at constant currency, with UK and Germany volumes rebounding +2% on promotion efficiency. Headwinds from EU sugar taxes and PFAS packaging regs are baked in, offset by +10% growth in plant-based dairy alternatives.
- Asia-Pacific/LatAm (15%): High-teens growth, led by India (PureHarvest mango lassi up 25%) and Brazil (energy drinks +18% on e-commerce). We're assuming neutral FX, but a 5% stronger BRL/INR supports the top end.
- China: Cautious flat-to-low-single growth amid soft out-of-home demand, but our localized go-to-market with Alibaba's Freshippo is gaining traction in premium RTD teas.

Strategic Insights and Risks: This guidance assumes no material worsening of geopolitical tensions impacting cocoa/coffee supply chains—currently priced in via +15% hedges—or U.S. recessionary pressures curbing at-home consumption. Upside levers include faster-than-expected velocity on our Q4 holiday lineup (e.g., limited-edition gingerbread NutriBars) and $100 million in incremental savings from our SAP S/4HANA ERP rollout, now 70% complete across 45 plants. Downside risks center on persistent labor inflation (guiding wage comp +4.5%) and potential tariff escalations on Mexican imports post-elections.

In summary, our raised EPS guidance reflects a resilient consumer franchise, robust cost discipline, and category-leading innovation in a $1.8 trillion global F&B market still growing mid-single digits. We're well-positioned to outperform, much like we have versus the S&P 500 Consumer Staples index over the past three years.

Today, I'd like to dive deep into our EBITDA margin performance, which came in at 19.2% for the quarter—up 140 basis points year-over-year from 17.8% in Q3 last year, and sequentially stronger by 50 basis points from Q2's 18.7%. On a full-year basis through Q3, our adjusted EBITDA margin stands at 18.9%, a solid 110 basis point expansion versus the prior year period. This marks our third consecutive quarter of margin accretion, underscoring the resilience of our operating model amid a volatile macro environment in the Food & Beverage sector.

Let me break this down by the key drivers, starting with the positives that propelled this outperformance.

Gross Margin Expansion: Pricing Discipline and Mix Shift. Our gross margin expanded by 220 basis points year-over-year to 38.5%, the strongest quarterly print in two years. This was primarily driven by our targeted pricing actions across 75% of our portfolio, netting a 7.2% price realization globally—ahead of the 6.5% we guided at the start of the year. In our Beverages segment, which represents 55% of net revenue, we successfully passed through 8-10% list price increases on core brands like our flagship carbonated soft drinks and ready-to-drink teas, similar to what we've seen peers like Coca-Cola and PepsiCo execute amid sustained consumer tolerance for premium pricing.

Mix was another tailwind, contributing 90 basis points to gross margin. We saw accelerated growth in high-margin premium SKUs—our plant-based dairy alternatives grew 22% organically, outpacing the category average of 15% per Nielsen data, while our functional beverage line delivered 28% growth with 45%+ gross margins. Conversely, we strategically de-emphasized low-margin private-label snacks, pruning 5% of our legacy packaged foods portfolio to focus on health-oriented offerings aligned with the $200 billion global better-for-you snacking trend.

Productivity and Supply Chain Efficiencies: Delivering $180 Million in Savings. Operationally, we captured $180 million in year-to-date productivity savings, equating to 210 basis points of margin benefit. Key initiatives included our Enterprise Supply Chain Optimization program, which leveraged AI-driven demand forecasting—reducing inventory levels by 12% and working capital days by 8—to mitigate the cocoa price surge, now up 65% year-to-date per Bloomberg commodity indices. In dairy, where we've locked in 70% of next year's volumes via forward contracts at 5% below spot, we offset a 15% input inflation through yield improvements in our cheese and yogurt plants, achieving 3% manufacturing productivity gains via automation retrofits similar to those at Danone's facilities.

SG&A leverage was equally impressive, with expenses as a percentage of revenue declining 70 basis points to 19.3%. This reflects zero-based budgeting across our go-to-market model, trimming 10% of non-core trade spend while reallocating to digital shelf analytics and e-commerce, where our DTC channels now contribute 18% of Beverages revenue—up from 12% last year.

Regional Commentary: Balanced Performance with North America Leading. Regionally, North America delivered a standout 21.5% EBITDA margin, up 200 basis points year-over-year, fueled by 9% pricing in snacks and beverages amid sticky inflation, plus robust volume in our away-from-home channels recovering to 95% of pre-pandemic levels. EMEA faced headwinds, with margins at 16.8%—flat YoY—due to 12% energy cost escalation from the Ukraine conflict's lingering effects and softer consumer sentiment in Germany and the UK, where private label penetration hit 28% per Kantar. However, our premium coffee pods grew 15% here through targeted loyalty programs. In APAC, margins expanded to 18.2% on 11% organic growth in ready-to-drink categories, benefiting from favorable FX tailwinds in AUD and IDR, though we absorbed 20% palm oil inflation via localized sourcing partnerships in Indonesia.

Headwinds and Mitigants. Of course, no quarter is without challenges. Input cost inflation totaled $250 million headwind, led by cocoa, dairy, and ocean freight rates still 30% above 2021 averages per Drewry indices. We also ramped marketing investment by 15% to 8.5% of revenue, supporting new product launches like our zero-sugar energy drink line targeting Gen Z, which drove 5% market share gains in the $50 billion segment. FX was a 40 basis point drag, primarily from a stronger USD impacting our 40% international revenue mix.

Strategic Insights and Outlook. Looking ahead, our 'Margin Momentum 2025' strategy positions us for sustained expansion. We're investing $300 million in sustainable sourcing—certifying 90% of cocoa via Rainforest Alliance partnerships by year-end, reducing long-term volatility—and advancing precision agriculture pilots in wheat supply chains to cut costs 5-7%. Digital transformation, including blockchain traceability for our supply chain, will yield another $100 million in savings next year. Competitively, we're gaining share versus incumbents like Mondelez in snacks through portfolio premiumization, with 60% of innovation pipeline now in high-margin, health-focused categories.

For Q4, we expect EBITDA margins of 19.5-20.0%, with full-year landing at 19.1%, a 130 basis point improvement. This trajectory supports our long-term target of 22%+ by 2026, driven by disciplined execution in a category where top-quartile peers like Unilever and Procter & Gamble have demonstrated 300+ basis point expansions over similar cycles.

As we dive into the details, I'd like to highlight one of our fastest-growing channels: e-commerce, which continues to be a key driver of our top-line momentum and a testament to our omnichannel strategy in the competitive Food & Beverage landscape.

In Q3, our total net sales reached $1.45 billion, up 9% year-over-year on both reported and organic bases, aligning with our guidance despite softer category volumes in center-store snacks amid inflationary pressures. Within this, e-commerce sales—spanning our direct-to-consumer platform, marketplace partnerships, and quick-commerce integrations—delivered $285 million, representing 22.3% of total net sales. That's up from 14.2% in Q3 2023 and a sequential increase from 20.1% in Q2. Year-to-date, e-commerce has contributed $780 million, or 21% of our nine-month total, underscoring its shift from a growth accelerator to a core revenue pillar.

Let me break down the growth dynamics. E-commerce sales surged 52% year-over-year in the quarter, outpacing our overall company growth by 5.8x and significantly ahead of the broader U.S. online grocery market, which NielsenIQ pegs at around 28% YoY growth for Q3. This was fueled by a 35% increase in active digital customers, reaching 4.2 million unique buyers, with repeat purchase rates climbing to 68%—a 12-point improvement—thanks to our loyalty program's refined RFM segmentation. Average order value rose 18% to $62, driven by bundling promotions on our high-margin plant-based beverages and protein snack lines, like the new NitroFuel energy shots that saw 120% e-com uptake versus brick-and-mortar.

Regionally, the story is equally compelling. In North America, which accounts for 62% of our e-commerce mix, sales grew 61% YoY to $177 million, propelled by our deepened Amazon integration—where we're now a top-10 F&B seller in the grocery vertical—and exclusive launches on Walmart+. Our DTC site, powered by Shopify Plus, captured 45% of NA e-com volume, with traffic up 40% via Google Performance Max campaigns targeting 'clean-label snacks.' Europe contributed 24% of the mix at $68 million, up 42% YoY despite VAT compliance headwinds; here, partnerships with Ocado and Carrefour's digital platforms have been pivotal, especially for our organic tea pods that align with the EU's Green Deal sustainability push. In APAC and emerging markets—now 14% of e-com—we posted explosive 75% growth to $40 million, led by Tmall in China for our adaptogen-infused drinks and Flipkart in India, where urban millennials are driving demand for functional beverages amid rising health consciousness post-COVID.

Technically, we've invested over $45 million YTD in our e-commerce stack to sustain this trajectory. Key initiatives include migrating to a headless commerce architecture with BigCommerce for faster load times—reducing cart abandonment by 22%—and deploying Adobe Commerce's AI personalization engine, which boosted conversion rates 15% through dynamic product recommendations. We've also rolled out our 'AquaBox' subscription service: 350,000 subscribers now, with 85% retention and LTV averaging $450, contributing 28% of DTC revenue at 55% gross margins—nearly double our wholesale take-rate.

Strategically, e-commerce isn't just about top-line; it's reshaping our P&L and innovation pipeline. Gross margins in this channel hit 48.2% in Q3, 1,200 bps above traditional retail, thanks to disintermediated supply chains and lower slotting fees. Fulfillment costs, while elevated at 12% of e-com sales due to cold-chain needs for our ready-to-drink lines, are trending down 8% sequentially via optimized 3PL partnerships with UPS Freight and Gopuff for same-day delivery in 150 U.S. metros. Data goldmine? Absolutely—e-com analytics have informed 60% of our new product pipeline, like the low-sugar kombucha variants launched last month based on zero-party data from 1.2 million post-purchase surveys.

Looking ahead, we're guiding e-commerce to 25-27% of FY2024 revenue, with ambitions for 30%+ by FY2026, in line with peers like Mondelez. Challenges remain—supply chain volatility for cocoa in our chocolate-coated nuts and returns management for shelf-stable items—but our $150 million capex plan, including micro-fulfillment centers in Atlanta and Rotterdam, positions us to capture share in a market projected by McKinsey to hit $250 billion globally for online F&B by 2027.

In summary, e-commerce is our highest-ROI growth engine, blending convenience, data, and premiumization to navigate a promotional-heavy industry.

Today, I'd like to dive deep into our organic revenue performance, which remains a cornerstone of our growth story at AquaPure Beverages. For those unfamiliar, organic revenue excludes the impact of acquisitions, divestitures, and foreign exchange fluctuations, giving you a pure read on our core business momentum through volume, mix, and pricing.

Overall, we delivered organic revenue growth of 6.8% in Q3, accelerating from 5.2% in Q2 and surpassing our guidance midpoint of 5-6%. This marks our strongest quarterly organic print in over two years, driven by a balanced contribution across pricing discipline (up 4.1%), favorable product mix (up 1.6%), and modest volume gains (up 1.1%). On a two-year stacked basis, we're now at +14.5%, outpacing the broader Food & Beverage category average of +11% per Nielsen and IRI data. This resilience amid persistent inflation and shifting consumer behaviors underscores the strength of our portfolio, which spans packaged snacks, ready-to-drink beverages, and plant-based proteins—segments where we've gained 120 basis points of market share YTD.

Let me break this down regionally, as geographic diversification is key to our strategy. We report across four core regions: North America, EMEA, APAC, and Latin America, which collectively represent 98% of our revenue base.

North America (52% of total revenue): Organic growth here was robust at 8.2%, fueled by premiumization trends and accelerated new product introductions. Pricing contributed 4.8%, reflecting our targeted hikes on high-margin items like our AquaPure Protein Bars and Zero-Sugar RTD line, which saw velocity increases of 12% in club channels like Costco and Sam's Club. Volume/mix added 3.4%, with standout performance from plant-based snacks—up 15%—capitalizing on the post-pandemic health wave. Distribution expansion added 200 basis points, with ACV for our core SKUs now at 92% in grocery, up from 87% last year. Key initiative: Our 'Clean Label Accelerator' program, investing $25 million in reformulations to hit 95% non-GMO across snacks by FYE, drove trial rates up 18% per SPINS data.

EMEA (24% of total revenue): Growth moderated to 3.9%, in line with expectations given macroeconomic headwinds. Pricing was the hero at 5.2%, as we lapped softer comps and implemented elasticity-tested increases on ambient shelf-stable products like our AquaPure Soups and RTE meals. Volume dipped slightly (-0.4%) due to volume deleveraging in value channels amid 8-10% food inflation in the UK and Germany, but we offset this with premium wins: our plant-based dairy alternatives grew 22%, gaining share in the €15 billion alt-dairy market. Strategically, we're leaning into e-commerce, where platforms like Ocado and Amazon Fresh contributed 25% of regional sales growth. Outlook here hinges on our sustainability push—our 'Farm-to-Table Traceability' blockchain pilot with Carrefour has boosted brand perception scores by 14 points.

APAC (15% of total revenue): This region was our growth engine at 9.4% organic, rebounding from China lockdowns with double-digit gains in Southeast Asia. Pricing held steady at 3.2%, focused on affordable premium like our low-sugar bubble tea RTDs, while volume/mix surged 6.2%—led by 28% growth in savory snacks in India, where we've expanded to 15,000 incremental points of distribution via kirana modernization partnerships. In China, post-reopening momentum in our hydration beverages has market share up 1.5 points to 7.2% per Kantar. Technical tailwind: Our $10 million investment in localized flavor R&D—e.g., yuzu-infused sparkling waters—yielded 35% sell-through rates in Japan, driving repeat purchases.

Latin America (7% of total revenue): Organic growth clocked in at 7.1%, propelled by volume recovery in beverages amid economic stabilization in Brazil and Mexico. Pricing rose 3.9% on staples like our AquaPure Aguas Frescas and powdered mixes, with mix uplift from premium coconut waters (up 19%). Volume grew 3.2%, benefiting from informal channel velocity gains—think tienditas and street vendors—where we've rolled out single-serve packs. A bright spot: Brazil's protein snack category exploded 25%, where our P2B hybrids captured 8% share. Risks here include FX volatility, but our hedging covers 85% of exposures.

Looking forward, we're guiding Q4 organic growth to 6-7%, implying full-year ~6.2%, ahead of consensus. This reflects sustained pricing power (targeting 3-4% into FY25), NPI cadence of 50+ launches, and efficiency from SKU rationalization—we've pruned 15% of low-velocity items to focus on 80/20 winners. Strategic insights: In F&B, where private label pressures and GLP-1 drug impacts loom (potentially shaving 1-2% volume next year), our edge lies in 'functional indulgence'—healthier indulgences like fiber-enriched chocolates. We're allocating 2.5% of sales to innovation, partnering with suppliers like ADM for upcycled ingredients to combat cocoa shortages.

For the full year, we are raising our guidance for adjusted EPS to $5.85 to $6.05, as detailed earlier.
